Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  slow growth / tariff reset
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  PMI upturn / ECB on hold
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  tariff relief / weak demand
🇦🇺 Australia  Mixed  hawkish RBA / soft consumer
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  cuts ahead / jobs softening
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
AI proof and cash returns get paid; beats alone do not
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Bitcoin stalls below $70,000 as stablecoins shrink
Bonds sell the tariff ruling, credit cracks widen
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
Tariff reset: replacement levy versus refunds
Tesla / TSLA  "retail buys what institutions sell"
TRUMP meme coin / TRUMP  "$4.3 billion of retail losses"
Robinhood / HOOD  "SpaceX and Stripe for retail"
body: Monday, February 23 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Growth disappointed and inflation did not: Q4 GDP rose just 1.4%, badly missing estimates, while inflation firmed at 3%. That mix keeps the Fed on hold with no room to cut. The tariff regime reset at the same time: the Supreme Court struck down Trump's global tariffs, and Trump answered with a new global levy, raised from 10% to 15%.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.48% and the 10Y at 4.08%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 60 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 13 bps and the 10Y 18 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more), leaving the curve positively sloped and approaching its long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-20). Treasuries fell after the ruling, while the S&P 500 rose 0.69% to 6,909.51 and the VIX fell 5.64% to 19.09 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

New / Most Important: Nvidia, Home Depot, banks and Berkshire report in the week ahead, alongside a Trump speech. Equities absorbed the tariff shock calmly, so the next move is more likely to come from Nvidia's guidance or an Iran strike than from trade policy.

Playbook ✓: Stay neutral on index beta and keep the rotation: overweight energy, industrials and materials, underweight application software and alternative managers. Keep duration neutral — weak growth favours bonds, but 3% inflation and lost tariff revenue cap the rally; add only if the 10Y backs up toward 4.26%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-20). An Iran strike argues for adding VIX hedges.

Macro Stance: Europe's cycle is turning up: euro-zone businesses performed better than expected in February as manufacturing bounced back, and German manufacturing grew for the first time since 2022. The STOXX 600 hit a record after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs.

Activity & Inflation: Inflation is not a constraint, with euro-zone inflation at 1.7% in January, so the ECB can stay on hold. The STOXX 600 closed at 630.56, up 3.65% over 20 sessions, while the DAX gained only 1.45% to 25,260.69 and EUR/USD slipped 0.84% over five sessions to 1.1769 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

New / Most Important: The risk is trade politics: the EU may freeze approval of its US trade deal over Trump's tariff 'chaos'. That keeps exporters' earnings visibility low even as domestic activity improves, and it argues for owning the cyclical recovery through domestically driven names.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Europe versus the US and add German cyclicals, where the PMI turn is fresh and the DAX has lagged the STOXX 600. Hedge export exposure with a short in autos. Cut the call if the EU–US deal collapses into retaliation or if the next PMI gives back the manufacturing gain.

Macro Stance: China is a relative winner from the US court ruling, and Trump plans to travel to China next month with tariffs in focus. Our view stays Mixed: external pressure is easing, but domestic demand, credit and property have not turned, and the equity rally is narrowing into AI names.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January, still in contraction. Xinhua reports steady growth in consumer spending over the Spring Festival holiday — supportive, but 'steady' is not the step-change a reflation call needs. The February PMIs are the next test; a move back above 50 would confirm that the holiday spending is broadening.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists. The feed carries no fresh total social financing print, so we read the credit impulse as flat at best: the seasonal January surge undershot. A turn needs household mortgage demand to recover, which the property data do not yet show; the February credit data are the next check.

Property: New-home prices extended their decline in January as weak demand hounds the sector. Policy support has slowed the slide in places but not reversed it, and developers remain dependent on restructurings rather than sales. Stay away from developers and their lenders until new-home price declines slow for consecutive months and mortgage demand picks up.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Xi's 2026 agenda prioritises domestic demand and tech independence, which steers support toward consumption and AI rather than another infrastructure push. On trade, the new US global levy applies to all partners, so China's relative tariff disadvantage narrows even though the absolute burden remains, and the planned Trump visit gives Beijing an incentive to keep the tone conciliatory.

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong reopened lower after the holiday: the Hang Seng lost 1.10% to 26,413.35 and is down 0.28% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), while the Shanghai Composite last closed at 4,082.07 before the break (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). In New York, ASHR rose 0.65% to 34.10 while KWEB is down 8.89% over 20 sessions at 32.70, and USD/CNY sits at 6.9081, down 0.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) — a steadily firmer yuan that eases outflow pressure.

New / Most Important: The rotation inside China tech is the story: AI startups surged after the holiday as money rotated out of big tech. Platform giants locked in subsidy wars lag, while model developers and AI hardware lead — the reverse of the US, where the AI scare trade is hitting software.

Playbook ✓: Own China AI and hardware exposure and prefer ASHR over KWEB's platform-heavy basket; add on dips into Trump's visit if trade headlines stay conciliatory. Cut if the visit is postponed or new-home prices keep falling into spring. ⚠ Divergence: the private PMI showed factory expansion accelerating in January, contradicting the official contraction and suggesting private manufacturers are faring better than the headline economy.

Macro Stance: Japan's policy mix is tilting reflationary: Takaichi is touting 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy to reassure markets, and Reuters reports the government's BOJ nominee list includes reflationists. With growth supported by fiscal policy and a weak yen, the BOJ can move slowly without losing control of inflation.

Activity & Currency: The yen's purchasing power has sunk to a 53-year low. USD/JPY rose 1.53% over five sessions to 155.16, while the Nikkei 225 fell 1.12% to 56,825.70 but is still up 5.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities with the currency hedged while USD/JPY trades near 155.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20); a reflationist BOJ slate is yen-negative and equity-positive. The risk is political pushback against the weak yen — The Japan Times calls a stronger yen Takaichi's next challenge — so lift the hedge if officials start talking the currency up.

Macro Stance: The RBA sees no set path after its February hike, with unemployment at 4.1% keeping talk of another rise alive. Yet business leaders and bankers warned that a recession could be the 'only way out'. A central bank leaning hawkish into a slowing consumer argues for Mixed.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7056, up 3.15% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 slipped 0.05% to 9,081.4 and is up 2.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). The currency is doing the tightening alongside the RBA, which caps imported inflation but squeezes exporters outside mining.

Playbook ✓: Keep AUD longs against the yen as the policy-rate gap widens, but stay neutral on the ASX with miners preferred over consumer names; copper's rise after the US tariff ruling helps the resource side. Turn bearish on domestic cyclicals if the next CPI print forces another hike.

Monetary & Activity: January CPI ran at 2.2% y/y, at target though above forecasts, keeping a March cut in play (Money.pl: 'Eksperci oceniają szanse na marcową obniżkę stóp' — experts weigh the odds of a March cut). The labour market is cracking: nearly 10 thousand jobs vanished, a drop wnp.pl says the market has not seen in decades ('Zniknęło niemal 10 tys. etatów').

FX & Markets: USD/PLN rose 1.06% over five sessions to 3.5871 and EUR/PLN 0.59% over 20 sessions to 4.2217, a mild softening as cut bets build. EPOL is up 1.48% over 20 sessions at 37.81 and the WIG20TR tracker 2.62% at 67.36. Pekao (PEO) is up 11.46% over 20 sessions at 232.40 and PKO BP (PKO) 2.31% over five at 91.40, while Allegro (ALE) fell 3.42% to 27.67 and LPP 4.43% over five sessions to 19,965 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Companies: Pekao topped profit estimates on higher fee income, showing lenders can grow fees as rates fall. Grupa Azoty is seeking an 83% debt writedown in its polymer restructuring, a reminder that the chemicals sector remains distressed.

Security & New Development: Poland withdrew from the treaty banning antipersonnel mines to defend against Russia, and Europe's main military powers will develop low-cost air-defence systems. Economists poured cold water on the SAFE loans (Money.pl: 'Kubeł zimnej wody ws. SAFE'), so the financing mix for the defence build-out remains contested.

Playbook ✓: Own Polish banks (PEO, PKO) for fee growth and receive Polish rates into a March cut; the jobs shock makes easing more likely, not less. Avoid domestic consumer names (ALE, LPP) until employment stabilises. ⚠ Divergence: Pekao is up 11.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) even as job losses hit a multi-decade extreme — bank equities price growth that the labour data no longer confirm.

Narrative: The AI-disruption trade has moved from software into security: cyber stocks slid as Anthropic unveiled a Claude security tool. XLK is down 2.76% over 20 sessions at 140.88, Microsoft 11.95% at 397.23, and Oracle fell 5.40% in the prior session to 148.08 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Reported: Earnings can still break the spell: beaten-down RingCentral and Five9 rallied as results quelled some AI concerns. The market pays for proof that AI adds to revenue rather than replacing seats.

EPS Upside Watch: Names that can show AI monetisation in their next prints — data infrastructure and AI-server vendors — have the best setups, while seat-based application software needs a guidance raise just to hold its level.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The hardware layer keeps winning while the application layer is sold: SMH is up 3.03% over 20 sessions as XLK falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). The contrarian long is quality software with proven AI revenue, funded by shorts in single-product cyber names.

Narrative: GOOGL jumped 4.01% to 314.98 and XLC rose 1.44% to 116.80 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), on the day the WSJ reported Google is exploring ways to use its financial might to take on Nvidia. Platforms with their own chips and cash flows are being re-rated as AI winners rather than AI spenders.

Reported: With the sector's earnings largely behind it, price action did the talking: META rose 1.69% to 655.66 and Netflix 2.17% to 78.67, though Netflix is still down 5.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet is the cleanest upside candidate if its chip ambitions turn into external revenue; Meta's ad engine monetises AI fastest among the spenders. Netflix's derating sets a lower bar for its next print if engagement holds.

⚡ Breaking Convention: If Google turns its chips into a merchant product, the largest communication-services name becomes a semiconductor competitor — a cross-sector risk for Nvidia and a re-rating driver that XLC holders own without paying for it.

Narrative: Private-credit stress is spreading from one manager to the asset class: two firms offered to buy shares in three Blue Owl private-credit funds at a big discount. XLF is down 2.45% over 20 sessions at 52.49 despite a 0.65% bounce in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Reported: Large US banks did not report in the window; bank results and Berkshire are on the week-ahead calendar. JPMorgan is up 2.36% over 20 sessions at 310.79 while Goldman is down 3.39% at 922.24 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), splitting balance-sheet lenders from capital-markets exposure.
EPS Upside Watch: Money-centre banks that can buy private-credit assets at a discount are the beneficiaries of forced selling; JPMorgan's relative strength already reflects that.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The 'shadow default' rate in the $3 trillion private-credit market is rising as more money chases lower-quality deals. If marks follow, the problem migrates from liquidity to losses — and to the banks that lend to these funds.

Narrative: Brent settled higher with a weekly gain on Iran–US jitters, closing at 71.76, up 6.28% over five sessions and 12.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). XLE is up 12.21% over 20 sessions at 54.88.

Reported: Occidental jumped as a $5.8 billion debt cut and dividend hike impressed investors, the template for what energy investors reward. Exxon fell 2.44% in the prior session to 147.28 even as Brent rose, while Chevron is up 10.36% over 20 sessions at 183.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

EPS Upside Watch: Upstream estimates follow Brent, now 12.02% above its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20); integrated majors with downstream exposure get the best of both if crude stays plentiful.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Analysts see a supply glut that has not translated into lower prices this year: the floor under crude is geopolitical. If Iran de-escalates, the glut reasserts itself quickly — own energy with a stop, not as a buy-and-hold.

Narrative: Industrials keep leading: XLI is up 7.09% over 20 sessions at 177.23, GE 16.35% at 343.22 and Caterpillar 17.17% at 759.74 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Physical capex — grid, aerospace, defence — is the market's preferred AI-proof growth.

Reported: Deere boosted its outlook and sees construction and small-agriculture demand recovering, extending the capex theme beyond data centres. GE rose 9.69% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) as aerospace demand holds.
EPS Upside Watch: Defence: Europe's main military powers will develop low-cost air-defence systems, a new procurement line for missile and drone-defence suppliers on both sides of the Atlantic.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Boeing is down 7.71% over 20 sessions at 232.03 despite strong order flow (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20): inside XLI, own engines and defence rather than the airframer.

Narrative: The tariff ruling is a direct discretionary catalyst: the retail industry calls the reversal a win, even as uncertainty remains. XLY rose 1.04% to 117.45 but is still down 4.22% over 20 sessions, and Amazon gained 2.56% to 210.11 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Reported: With few large discretionary prints in the window, price action did the talking: Nike gained 7.04% over five sessions to 65.40, while Tesla is down 8.35% over 20 sessions at 411.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). The market is rewarding turnaround stories and punishing narrative-driven valuations.

EPS Upside Watch: Importers with large tariff bills — furniture, toys, apparel — gain most if refunds flow, but the replacement levy offsets part of the benefit. Home Depot, up 0.97% to 382.25 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), reports in the week ahead with lower mortgage rates as its tailwind.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Because a replacement levy is already in place, tariff relief is partial: the trade is in refund cash, not lower ongoing costs. Equal-weight retail is the cleaner expression than Amazon-heavy XLY.

Narrative: Staples are crowded: XLP is up 6.83% over 20 sessions at 87.89 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), and staples leading with the S&P 500 near record highs has rarely ended well, per The Motley Fool.

Reported: Walmart's new CEO began with a cautious outlook after another quarter of steady sales; WMT fell 7.97% over five sessions to 122.99 and Costco 1.36% to 985.27 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

EPS Upside Watch: Household and personal-care names with pricing power can still beat; packaged food looks more exposed, in our view, to volume-led estimate cuts, so the downside risk to numbers sits there.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Tariff refunds favour retailers with large import bills over staples makers, which could flip the defensive rotation; fund XLP trims into equal-weight retail and large-cap pharma.

Narrative: Healthcare remains a stock picker's market: XLV is down 0.93% over 20 sessions at 156.82, with Eli Lilly down 7.16% and UnitedHealth 18.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Drug-pricing risk looks contained in our view, but managed care is still digesting its reset.
Reported: Grail has plunged 50% despite an earnings beat, proof that in diagnostics and biotech the pipeline outranks the quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: The world's largest hedge fund bought UnitedHealth; at 290.00 after an 18.19% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), managed care has the lowest bar for positive revisions.

⚡ Breaking Convention: With staples crowded, large-cap pharma is the cheapest defensive left: steady cash flows without the rotation premium now embedded in XLP. Lilly's 7.16% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) offers an entry into a quality franchise on weakness rather than strength.

Narrative: Copper climbed as the Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs, rising 1.76% to 5.83, while gold front-month gained 1.67% to 5,080.90 and silver 6.08% to 82.28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). XLB is up 6.95% over 20 sessions at 52.96, with AI data-centre and grid demand the structural driver for copper.
Reported: Freeport rose 2.83% to 64.34 and is up 9.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20): copper producers are re-rating with the metal as trade friction eases.

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners: JPMorgan raised its gold forecast to $6,300 and makes a case for $8,000. Newmont fell 2.61% to 122.13 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), lagging the metal — a catch-up candidate.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver's 8.92% gain over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) reverses part of its slide, but its swings are too violent for a core position; own copper and gold miners instead.

Narrative: Mortgage rates hit their lowest level since September 2022, and XLRE is up 5.88% over 20 sessions at 43.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Rate relief is real, and REITs are trading as bond proxies again as long yields stall.

Reported: Few REIT prints landed in the window, so the macro tape is the report card: the 10Y's 18 bps decline over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-20) has eased funding costs, but weak Q4 growth limits the pass-through to rents and occupancy.
EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and tower REITs remain the earnings-growth pocket; residential landlords and brokers need transaction volumes to recover before lower rates show up in earnings.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lower mortgage rates have not yet unlocked housing turnover, so the better real-estate trade is land-rich and data-centre owners rather than residential REITs waiting for volume. A pickup in transactions would be the signal to rotate back into residential names.

Narrative: XLU is up 8.48% over 20 sessions at 46.33 and Constellation 6.78% over five sessions at 294.84 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20): data-centre load growth is turning regulated utilities into compounders.
Reported: Southern raised its spending plan to $81B as load grows — rate-base growth that translates into higher long-run EPS.

EPS Upside Watch: Utilities with transmission-heavy plans and IPPs with contract optionality such as Vistra and Constellation have the clearest upgrade path as hyperscaler deals are signed. Vistra is up 6.88% over 20 sessions at 171.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), trailing the sector ETF and leaving room to catch up on the next contract.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Data-centre developers are building private natural-gas 'shadow grid' plants to sidestep strained grids. If that spreads, regulated utilities lose part of the load growth they are being valued on — favour generators and gas-turbine suppliers over pure wires.

Narrative: Europe's car sales fell 3.6% in January as Chinese brands surged, the share-loss problem in one line. EXV5 rose 0.48% to 46.17 and is up 1.05% over 20 sessions, while Stellantis is down 21.04% over 20 sessions at 7.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).
Reported: Aston Martin issued another profit warning and sold its F1 naming rights for £50m, the latest sign that low-volume luxury makers cannot price their way out of weak demand.

EPS Upside Watch: Self-help remains the only lever; BMW, up 3.08% over 20 sessions at 90.32, and Mercedes, up 1.61% at 59.24, lead the group (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) on cost delivery rather than volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Chinese brands gaining share in a shrinking market means pricing, not volume, is the battleground; a long BMW, short Stellantis pair isolates the winners from the share donors.

Narrative: Memory is the AI choke point, says Google DeepMind's chief executive. SOXX is up 3.09% over 20 sessions at 359.43, TSMC rose 2.82% to 370.54 and Micron 2.59% to 428.17, while AMD is down 21.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Reported: The sector's next estimate reset is Nvidia's report on Feb. 25; ASML is up 4.46% over five sessions at 1,469.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) as equipment names price in more capacity.
EPS Upside Watch: Memory makers and equipment suppliers see price-driven upgrades while shortages persist; AI-server builders gain volume but face memory-cost pressure on margins.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Trump took aim at Taiwan's chip sector after the Supreme Court ruling: a new tariff risk for TSMC just as the broader tariff regime eased. Hedge TSM longs with SOXX puts into any announcement.
Rewarded: Results that disproved the AI-disruption thesis or raised the outlook: RingCentral and Five9 rallied as earnings quelled AI concerns, and Deere jumped on a higher outlook.

Punished: Beats without a better outlook were sold: Walmart's cautious guidance overshadowed steady sales, and Grail has plunged 50% despite beating. Consumer-facing and AI-exposed services needed a guidance raise, not just a beat, to hold their gains.

Pattern: The market pays for forward visibility in the physical economy and in AI hardware, and for software that can show AI adds revenue. It discounts beats in businesses exposed to AI substitution or to cautious consumers, and it rewards capital discipline over volume growth.

Attention into EPS: Nvidia on Feb. 25 is the event, but Bloomberg argues the stock is so stuck that even blowout earnings may not lift it; NVDA closed at 189.82, up 2.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Home Depot, banks and Berkshire also report in the week ahead.

Playbook: Into reports, buy names where guidance risk is skewed up — equipment, memory, industrial capex — and sell beats in seat-based software and consumer platforms that lack guidance raises. Treat a beat-and-hold as a sell signal in crowded defensives.

Attention Gap: The Supreme Court left the fate of billions in tariff money already paid unsettled, and the market's attention is on the replacement levy rather than on potential refunds. A refund would be a one-off cash windfall for importers with large tariff bills, and analysts have little reason to model it until a refund process exists.

Exposure & Risk: Express through equal-weight retail (XRT) and importers of furniture, toys and apparel. Risk: refund timing and eligibility are uncertain until the courts or the administration set out a process, and the new global levy keeps ongoing costs elevated.

Attention Gap: German manufacturing grew for the first time since 2022, yet the DAX is up only 1.45% over 20 sessions against 3.65% for the STOXX 600 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Investors still treat Germany as Europe's laggard.

Exposure & Risk: Express through EWG or DAX futures, tilted to capital goods and automation rather than autos. Risk: an EU freeze of the US trade deal and the new US levy could hit exporters before domestic orders recover.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 67,659.39, down 0.51% on the day and 14.02% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,957.81, down 16.49%, and Solana at 82.79, down 20.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-22). Equities tied to crypto bounced: Coinbase rose 21.45% over five sessions to 171.35, MSTR 6.54% to 131.05 and IBIT 3.70% to 38.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin gained but quickly retreated after the tariffs were ruled illegal, so even a macro relief event could not hold a rally. Tether's USDT is set for its biggest monthly retreat since the FTX collapse — shrinking stablecoin supply means less dry powder on exchanges.

Playbook: Stay underweight crypto beta until ETF flows turn and stablecoin supply stops shrinking; those are the two inputs that have to change before spot can rally. Prefer COIN over spot for rebound exposure, since the equity has already turned, and buy downside protection on bitcoin while USDT supply contracts.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 97.80, up 0.90% over five sessions but down 0.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). Treasuries fell after the Supreme Court scrapped the tariffs: the 10Y held at 4.08%, down only 1 bp over five observations, while TLT slipped 0.23% to 89.41 (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-20; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).

Credit Check: Public credit is steady — HYG at 81.00 and LQD at 111.59 are little changed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20) — but the private market is repricing, with discount bids for Blue Owl fund shares and a rising shadow default rate.

Portfolio Implication: US stocks drew their lowest share of global flows since 2020, per BofA; we stay overweight Europe and Japan and neutral US. Keep duration neutral, prefer investment grade to high yield, and avoid semi-liquid private-credit vehicles until secondary discounts narrow.

What Is Priced: Trump says he is considering a limited military strike on Iran, yet the VIX fell 5.64% to 19.09 while Brent sits at 71.76, up 12.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). OilPrice argues traders may be pricing Iran risk too lightly.

Conditional Expression: If a strike comes, own Brent call spreads, XLE and defence, and short airlines and EUR/USD. If a deal is reached, the premium built over 20 sessions unwinds: take profits on energy and rotate into airlines, discretionary and European cyclicals.
Risk: Timing is binary and headline-driven, and a supply glut that has not yet hit prices caps the upside if no barrels are lost. Use options, not futures, and size for a weekend gap.

What Is Priced: The S&P 500 rose 0.69% after the ruling (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20), pricing relief, while Trump has already raised the replacement global levy from 10% to 15%. The market assumes partners stay in their deals.

Conditional Expression: If partners hold their deals and refunds flow, buy importers, equal-weight retail and European exporters. If the EU freezes its deal and retaliation follows, short European autos and US importers and add to gold.
Risk: The replacement levy can change again by announcement, so position with short-dated options and keep sizes modest until the legal basis for the new tariffs is clear.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25. Bloomberg notes the stock is so stuck that even blowout earnings may not lift it — which is why the setup is attractive: expectations for a re-rating are low while memory shortages signal demand still outruns supply.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 189.82, up 1.02% in the prior session and 2.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20). The thesis breaks if guidance fails to lift data-centre expectations or if Google's push into chips becomes a pricing threat.

Catalyst & Thesis: Two firms offered to buy shares in three Blue Owl private-credit funds at a big discount, while the shadow default rate in private credit is rising. Secondary bids below net asset value challenge the marks that underpin fees; until redemption pressure eases, the shares stay a short.

Price Hurdle & Risk: OWL is not on our price card; the hurdle is a narrowing of the secondary discount. Risk: a well-bid asset sale or a bank buyer for the loans could quickly reassure investors and squeeze shorts.

Catalyst & Thesis: Dell reports in the week ahead, and the world's largest hedge fund bought Dell stock. AI-server demand from enterprises and neoclouds should drive the guide, and the memory shortage supports pricing on high-end systems.
Price Hurdle & Risk: DELL is not on our price card; the hurdle is a raised AI-server backlog. Risk: memory costs squeeze PC and server margins faster than Dell can reprice.
Observed Attention: Retail investors are piling into Tesla as institutional investors sell; TSLA closed at 411.82, down 8.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).
Motivation & Bias: Retail buys the autonomy and AI narrative and the dip in a familiar name; the bias is anchoring to past highs while institutions focus on auto fundamentals.
Instrument & Risk: Use defined-risk call spreads rather than leveraged ETFs; the risk is that auto fundamentals, not narrative, set the next leg.
Observed Attention: Opendoor surged again, with Barron's calling it a meme-stock favourite, as falling mortgage rates give retail traders a housing-recovery story to chase.
Motivation & Bias: The hook is leverage to a housing recovery at a low share price; the bias is extrapolating a rate-driven bounce before housing turnover has actually recovered.
Instrument & Risk: Small position or call spreads only; meme moves reverse fast, and a failed housing pickup leaves the iBuying model exposed to inventory losses.
Observed Attention: The TRUMP and MELANIA meme coins have left retail investors with a $4.3 billion loss, a measure of how much speculative capital chased political tokens.
Motivation & Bias: Buyers were chasing proximity to power and viral momentum; the bias is treating a celebrity token as a policy bet rather than a pure sentiment asset.
